newsitem.title: CHINA: China calls for boost in anti-drug education.
newsitem.headline: China calls for boost in anti-drug education.

text.p: Most of China's drug addicts are young people and officials should strengthen anti-drug education among them to halt the spread of abuse, the People's Daily said on Tuesday.
"Drugs are not only a problem leading some young people astray but also a big problem linked with the rise and fall of our people and our nation," the newspaper said.
Among registered drug addicts, those under 35 years old accounted for 80 percent and those under 25 for 65 percent, the newspaper said.
The newspaper blamed the rising number of young drug addicts on China's poor anti-drug education.
A survey of 55 middle school students in southern Guangzhou city showed 14.5 percent were willing to try drugs once or twice, it said.
Another survey revealed 86 percent of young people used drugs for the first time out of curiosity and were unaware of the dangers, the newspaper said, without elaborating.

Drug abuse, once effectively eradicated under the stern puritan rule of Chairman Mao Zedong, has increased in China following economic reforms that have loosened the central government's control over society.
Drug addiction in China has soared in recent years, with the latest figures showing the number of registered addicts jumping to 520,000 in 1995 from 148,000 in 1991, the newspaper said.
Chinese drug experts have said the total number of addicts could be as high as one million, with most now favouring heroin over opium, once China's traditional narcotic of choice.
